bullets.title: NVIDIA China Chip: Small-Batch Shipments of Export-Compliant AI Chip by Year-End
bullets.body: NVIDIA is planning small-batch shipments of a new AI chip designed specifically for Chinese customers by end of 2026. The chip is a China-specific LPU variant that works alongside GPUs to accelerate processing, complies with US export controls, and has already attracted orders from several Chinese customers. Whether Beijing will permit orders remains unclear.

bullets.title: NVDA/ORCL Hyperscaler CDS Blowing Out to All-Time Wide Spreads
bullets.body: Credit spreads on major hyperscalers are widening sharply, with ORCL and NVDA at all-time wide CDS levels and META approaching records. One fintwit account notes the 'post-July rip is over' as market structure stress signals emerge beyond just equity prices.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Racks Now Live at OpenAI; CoreWeave Deal with HRT
bullets.body: The first NVIDIA Vera Rubin racks are now powering OpenAI's training infrastructure. Separately, Hudson River Trading signed a multi-billion compute deal with CoreWeave to run AI research on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX B200 GPUs — HRT becomes one of the first Vera Rubin customers.

bullets.title: NVDA Foundry Strategy: Likely to Reduce TSMC Dependency vs. Prior Cycle
bullets.body: Informed semiconductor analyst notes NVIDIA shifted from ~70% internal production (Pico/Hopper era) to external sourcing for Rubin compute tiles, having previously flagged margin headwinds from external foundry reliance. Analyst questions whether NVIDIA will return to prior TSMC volume levels.

bullets.title: INTC Nova Lake-S Power Draw 2.4x Expected TDP; Foundry Margin Risk if IO-Tile-Only
bullets.body: Intel's 28-core Nova Lake-S reportedly draws 296W PL1 vs. a 125W expected TDP — a 2.4x overshoot raising efficiency concerns. Separately, a well-sourced analyst warns Intel foundry margins would 'absolutely crater' if limited to IO tiles; the strategy requires in-house compute tiles to be viable.

bullets.title: TSMC Offloads 30-Year Fab Overcapacity Risk to Big Tech Customers
bullets.body: Commentary from a credible analyst highlights that TSMC has effectively transferred the risk of fab overcapacity to major tech customers, who 'didn't fully appreciate the extent' of that risk transfer. TSMC expects its fab infrastructure to run for 30 years.

bullets.title: Optical Sector (AAOI, COHR): Severely Capacity-Constrained Despite Underperformance
bullets.body: A fintwit analyst argues the optical sector is 'severely capacity-constrained' with 'exceptional demand visibility' — AAOI and Coherent combined are still struggling to meet customer demand. However, a separate analyst cautions against overestimating optical attach rates and warns manufacturing constraints will delay deployment timelines.

bullets.title: FN: Rosenblatt Reiterates Buy/$750 PT; NOK Now 11% of Revenue
bullets.body: Rosenblatt reiterated a Buy and $750 PT on Fabrinet post-earnings with the stock around $440 — implying ~70% upside. A separate note flags that Nokia now represents 11% of FN's entire revenue, an emerging concentration to watch.

bullets.title: MU: $250B+ US Investment Announced; $10B Research Labs; Employee Stock Speculation
bullets.body: Micron announced it will invest more than $250B in US advanced memory manufacturing and R&D over the coming years, expected to create 90K+ jobs. The company also unveiled a new Micron Gigaresearch Lab with $10B dedicated to memory and compute breakthroughs. The scale of the investment sparked fintwit speculation on employee equity monetization.

bullets.title: BABA AI Revenue Approaching $10B Annualized; In-House Chips to Lift Margins
bullets.body: Alibaba guided AI-product annualized revenue to approach $10B next quarter from a current ~$7.3B run rate (~37% sequential growth). The company also expects 'substantially higher' gross margins and profitability as its own AI chips replace purchased chips in data centers, with AI investment payback shortening toward 2.5 years.

bullets.title: META Quietly Becomes One of MSFT's Largest AI Customers
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports Meta has quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers. Meta is also heading to trial over allegations it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict young users while concealing child safety risks.

bullets.title: SMCI: Independent Probe Finds No Evidence of Sanctioned-Party Sales; Shares +1.6% Premarket
bullets.body: Supermicro completed an independent investigation and found no proof that current senior management was aware of any alleged diversion scheme, and no direct sales to banned parties were identified. Terminated employees were cited for rule violations. Shares rose 1.6% in premarket on the news; the board also approved export compliance improvements.

bullets.title: NET: 30%+ Growth But Supply Chain Analysis Flags Warning Sign
bullets.body: Two posts flag Cloudflare growing 30%+ annually but warn that custom supply chain mapping across NET, Akamai, Fastly, hyperscalers, and neoclouds reveals a warning sign — competitive power and profits may not be accruing to Cloudflare as investors expect.

bullets.title: GOOGL/Waymo: 1.4M Monthly Rides in California, 10x Growth; Custom 5nm ASIC Chip Revealed
bullets.body: Waymo is now executing over 1.4 million monthly rides in California, a 10x increase over two years. The company also revealed for the first time a purpose-built 5nm ASIC chip for robotaxi ML inference as part of broader custom component development.

bullets.title: TSLA Robotaxi: 170 Unsupervised Austin Rides Completed Over Two Weeks
bullets.body: All 170 Tesla Robotaxi rides in Austin over the past two weeks were unsupervised, per monitoring by Robo Report. Separate fintwit commentary on FSD competitive dynamics notes advanced AI will eventually lower barriers to FSD creation, eroding current competitive advantages.

bullets.title: MDB: Unusual ~$2M OTM Call Purchase Flags Upside Speculation
bullets.body: Traders flagged approximately $2M in far out-of-the-money call options on MongoDB, suggesting positioning for a significant upside move ahead.

bullets.title: Bessent Treasury Intervention: Buyback Gains Erased; JPM/$GS Critical
bullets.body: US 30-year Treasury yields erased all gains from Bessent's buyback announcement, with the 30Y yield rising 6bp to 5.25% and 10Y breaking above 4.70%. JPMorgan warned the market would view Treasury as 'lacking credibility,' Goldman characterized the move as a 'band-aid on a bullet hole' driven by fiscal fears not technical factors, and Nomura said losing the long-end is 'unacceptable.' Bessent signaled buybacks could exceed the announced $4B.

bullets.title: SPY: Millions in OTM Puts at the Open for Third Consecutive Day; $3.1B Put Wall at 765
bullets.body: For the third consecutive day, traders accumulated millions in out-of-the-money SPY puts at the market open. A $3.1B put wall sits at the 765 strike, suggesting significant downside hedging activity building in the market.

bullets.title: US Debt Hits $40T; Bessent Signals Deficit Has Peaked; JPM Forecasts $3.5T Funding Gap
bullets.body: US national debt crossed $40 trillion for the first time, with the last $1T added in 152 days and daily deficit spending at $6.58B. Bessent stated there is a 'very good chance' the fiscal deficit has peaked and argued the US can 'grow our way' out of debt. JPMorgan countered by forecasting a $3.5T+ funding gap in coming fiscal years requiring more duration supply, not less.

bullets.title: Philly Fed Smashes Estimates at 47.4; Jobless Claims Beat at 206K; Leading Index +0.2%
bullets.body: August Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index came in at 47.4 vs. a 24.8 estimate and 41.4 prior — the largest monthly jump in the survey's 56-year history. Initial jobless claims declined to 206K vs. 210K expected, and the Conference Board Leading Economic Index rose 0.2% vs. 0.1% estimate. Prices paid eased to 40.9 from 53.9.
